doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Ellington's music and young players missing dance work
summary: Williams regrets young rhythm players never played for dancing every night.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well things about Ellington said, or someone said it anyway, Ellington is forever. I think the music is forever.

The only regret that I really have, and I hope somebody will take care of it, the young people today coming up playing music and playing rhythm instruments particularly, not wind instruments so much, never had that experience of playing for dancing.

And when we had to do it, every single night. And you had to have it right. It is an exact thing that we do. It is flexible, but it’s still exact. That tempo, and the time, and the feel, the feeling that is given. It’s something that they missed altogether. I mean a lot of the young people they missed it altogether in big bands, in fact they get together now and
they have six pieces, seven pieces and a synthesizer, and electric doodads and they make noises, but they’re not breathing noises.
